title: Temporary Heaters and Ventilation During Flooring Work
summary: Cold weather often means temporary heaters in rooms where adhesives and finishes are used. This talk covers OSHA's ventilation, clearance and fuel rules for temporary heating devices.
talking_points: Fresh air must be supplied in sufficient quantities to maintain the health and safety of workers. Where natural means are inadequate, provide mechanical ventilation (29 CFR 1926.154(a)(1)).
When heaters are used in confined spaces, take special care to provide enough ventilation for proper combustion, worker health and safety, and to limit temperature rise (1926.154(a)(2)).
Temporary heaters must be installed with at least the clearance to combustible material shown in Table F-4, unless listed for less (1926.154(b)(1)-(2)).

Heaters not suitable for wood floors must not be set directly on them or on other combustibles. They must rest on suitable heat insulating material or at least 1 inch of concrete, extending 2 feet or more in all directions (1926.154(b)(3)).
Heaters must be at least 10 feet from combustible tarps, canvas or similar coverings, and the coverings must be fastened securely (1926.154(b)(4)).
Heaters must be set level unless the manufacturer allows otherwise (1926.154(c)). Solid fuel salamanders are prohibited in buildings and on scaffolds (1926.154(d)).
Flammable liquid-fired heaters must have a primary safety control that stops fuel flow on flame failure (1926.154(e)(1)).

Category 1, 2 or 3 flammable liquids may be used only where there are no open flames or other ignition sources within 50 feet of the operation (1926.152(f)(3)). Check where heaters are before opening adhesive.
site_hazards_to_check: Heater near adhesive, solvent or rags
Heater too close to combustibles or tarps
Closed room with a fuel-burning heater
Heater sitting on a wood subfloor
Solid fuel salamander in a building
discussion_questions: Where will heaters be while adhesives are in use?
How do we get fresh air into this room?
Who checks heater clearances at the start of the shift?
